answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded work history: instead of counting identities, the network weights each agent by staked collateral plus a verifiable record of peer-attested useful work. Anyone can spawn thousands of hollow shells for free, but each shell must forge a genuine history of real contributions before it earns any voting weight — like a lantern that only gives light after it has burned fuel. An attacker can mint unlimited identities but cannot mint time, stake, or honest peer approval at scale, so the marginal cost of the attack rises with every fake seat they try to take.
